1. The animation shows the idea that paying extra on a mortgage earns a guaranteed return equal to the loan's interest rate. At the Oct 8, 2026 survey rate that is 7.40% a year, before taxes. A character named Tessa, labeled "illustrative," has a house and a bill of cash. The cash is set against a bar at 7.40%, measured up from zero.

2. Tessa and her house stay put, while the cash and the bar move around the screen and gain labels. In frame 1 the cash is next to the house. In frame 2 a bar appears above it with a bill on top. In frame 3 the bar is labeled "the bar: 7.40% a year, before taxes," with a scale from zero to 7.40%. In frame 4 the label "interest no longer charged" is added. In frame 5 a dashed, faded bill appears with the label "any other use." In frame 6 that label gains the words "not tested." The footer in every frame reads "US only · history, not a forecast."

3. Putting cash toward the mortgage saves interest that would otherwise be charged, which works like earning 7.40% a year with no risk. The dashed "any other use," such as investing, is the alternative. It would need to beat that 7.40% bar to come out ahead. The animation does not say whether any alternative would do that, and "not tested" says it was not checked.

4. The animation gives no explicit advice. A viewer could infer that 7.40% is the hurdle any other use of the cash has to clear. It does not tell them to prepay or to invest.

5. The animation did not suggest any advice, so the answer to question 4 is only my reading of the bar comparison. The picture and text show the 7.40% bar and say other uses are "not tested," and they stop short of a recommendation.
